concerns.concern: With only a ~3 s cycle, the device may never return to its insulating state. Persistent metallic regions could build up and make successive On images correlated without any deterministic filament re-formation. Off-state resistance versus cycle, off-phase images and V(t) traces are needed.
concerns.quote: With a duty cycle of only ~3 s, the device may never return to its insulating configuration.

concerns.concern: A single τ is fitted across all aging times while β is allowed to vary. If τ itself ages, β is forced to absorb the change, so the β evolution that defines 'jamming' could be a fitting artifact. Independent τ and β fits per aging time are needed.
concerns.quote: The β(t_age) evolution in Fig. 4 could therefore be partly or wholly an artifact of the constrained fit.

concerns.concern: Most extracted relaxation times far exceed the measurement window, so τ and β are strongly covariant and the decay is tiny. The quoted uncertainties seem implausibly small; full covariance or confidence intervals and the error-estimation method are needed.
concerns.quote: The quoted uncertainties (e.g. ±100 s on 24,000 s, ±3000 s on 81,000 s) seem implausibly small.

concerns.concern: The claimed train/reset capability is not shown. Sub-threshold erasure was tested only on the as-prepared state, not on a trained one. The full train, erase, verify and retrain sequence must be demonstrated or the claim toned down.
concerns.quote: the sub-threshold erasure experiment (Fig. 3a) was performed on the *initial, as-prepared* state, not on a trained/jammed state.

concerns.concern: No electrical measure of switching stochasticity is presented, such as threshold distributions, delay times or On-resistance variance. Whole-area speckle correlation is not equivalent to deterministic filament location or timing.
concerns.quote: The claim that "switching becomes deterministic" needs an electrical correlate.

concerns.concern: Control experiments are missing: the same synchronized protocol with sub-threshold pulses, and with no current at all (detector gating only).
concerns.quote: the same synchronized protocol applied with sub-threshold pulses; the same protocol with no current at all, gating only the detector.

concerns.concern: Several effects could raise inter-image correlation over ~10³ s independent of domain learning: gradual thermal equilibration of substrate and stage, thermal-expansion peak shifts and sample drift. Peak position, intensity and width versus time and cycle, and any drift correction, should be reported.
concerns.quote: The authors should report Bragg peak position, integrated intensity, and peak width versus time and cycle number, and state the drift correction used, if any.

concerns.concern: Compressed exponentials (β≈1.5) are generally attributed to ballistic, stress-driven relaxation and occur in many systems, so they are not by themselves a signature of a jamming transition.
concerns.quote: Compressed relaxation alone is not a signature of a jamming transition.

concerns.concern: Alternative mechanisms are not considered: strain-mediated coarsening, defect-pinned aging, or a slow approach to thermal steady state. The jamming interpretation needs supporting evidence, in particular a τ(q) analysis to distinguish ballistic from diffusive dynamics.
concerns.quote: The authors should analyze τ(q) across the detector ROI; it is the standard XPCS test distinguishing ballistic from diffusive dynamics

concerns.concern: At 4 mA, β scatters with large error bars and never reaches the jammed value of 1.5. The sigmoid plateau is assumed rather than observed, leaving t_jam essentially unconstrained.
concerns.quote: The sigmoid plateau is assumed rather than observed, and t_jam = 4000 ± 3000 s is essentially unconstrained.

concerns.concern: There is a conceptual inconsistency: the sub-threshold current drives jamming fastest, yet it is presented as the erasing operation, while jamming is said to enable plastic memory.
concerns.quote: it is unclear why sub-threshold current, which jams the system fastest, is the erasing operation. This needs to be reconciled.

concerns.concern: The nearly coincident M1 and R reflections cannot separate decorrelation from domain rearrangement, strain redistribution within one phase, or uniform lattice expansion from heating. The last of these can mimic decorrelation; peak centroid monitoring and drift-corrected correlation are suggested.
concerns.quote: The last of these shifts the speckle pattern in q and can mimic decorrelation.

concerns.concern: The beam is larger than the 5×5 µm² device, so unbiased or heat-affected film outside the channel contributes speckle. The fraction of scattering from the active channel should be estimated.
concerns.quote: The fraction of scattering originating from the active channel should be estimated.

concerns.concern: Only a single training run on a single device appears to be shown. The reproducibility of the ~200-cycle onset, its dependence on current and duty cycle, and its behaviour in pristine devices should be stated quantitatively in the main text.
concerns.quote: It appears that a single training run on a single device is shown. How reproducible is the ~200-cycle onset?

concerns.concern: Hours of intense X-ray exposure on one spot could induce changes such as oxygen vacancies. The unbiased room-temperature control does not cover bias or elevated temperature.
concerns.quote: beam-induced changes (e.g. oxygen vacancy creation, known to affect VO₂) could contribute.

concerns.concern: Equation 1 omits pixel averaging and the standard normalization. Normalizing by time-averaged ⟨I²⟩ conflates total intensity changes with speckle decorrelation; the ROI, q-range and exact normalization must be specified.
concerns.quote: Normalizing by a time-averaged ⟨I²⟩ makes G sensitive to changes in total intensity (e.g. phase-fraction changes)

concerns.concern: The room-temperature τ is described by the authors as possibly reflecting the experimental stability limit, yet it is used as a data point in the Arrhenius fit.
concerns.quote: It is then inconsistent to use it as a data point in the Arrhenius fit.

concerns.concern: The Arrhenius fit appears to rest on very few temperatures. The number of temperatures measured should be stated and all fits shown.
concerns.quote: The Arrhenius fit appears to rest on very few temperatures.

concerns.concern: The 340 K data lie in the middle of the transition, where the authors themselves say the system is non-stationary, so fitting a single stationary τ there is questionable.
concerns.quote: Fitting a single stationary τ there is questionable.

concerns.concern: For the 0.26 and 1.7 mA conditions, the β transition is defined by very few data points.
concerns.quote: For 0.26 and 1.7 mA, the transition is defined by very few points.

concerns.concern: Several β values lie below 1, implying stretched, heterogeneous dynamics in the authors' framework, but this is not discussed.
concerns.quote: Several points lie below β = 1, which in the authors' framework would correspond to stretched (heterogeneous) dynamics. This is not discussed.

concerns.concern: The shear-thickening analogy is inverted. Stronger current delays jamming here, which resembles drive-induced fluidization rather than thickening.
concerns.quote: Here, stronger current *delays* jamming, which is closer to drive-induced fluidization (shear thinning or yielding).

concerns.concern: The claim that observing jamming in hard matter is remarkable ignores prior XPCS work on metallic glasses, antiferromagnetic, CDW and orbital domains, and the authors' own LSCO work.
concerns.quote: The statement that observing jamming "in hard matter" is "remarkable" should acknowledge prior XPCS work on hard condensed matter

concerns.concern: The text says domain speeds are obtained from the correlation decay as described in the Methods, but no speeds are reported and the Methods contain no such description.
concerns.quote: no speeds are reported and the Methods contain no such description.

concerns.concern: The coherence length (1.7 µm) is much smaller than the illuminated area, so the claim that coherent diffraction encodes the full real-space distribution should be qualified.
concerns.quote: The statement that coherent diffraction "encode[s] the full real-space distribution information" of the device should be qualified accordingly.

concerns.concern: Comparing an activation energy expressed in kelvin to the melting temperature of VO₂ is not physically meaningful. The associated argument about domains becoming freely mobile should be removed or justified.
concerns.quote: Comparing an activation energy expressed in kelvin (2700 K) to the melting temperature of VO₂ (2240 K) is not physically meaningful

concerns.concern: The activation energy should instead be compared with relevant energy scales, such as domain-wall motion, oxygen-vacancy migration, or the latent heat per formula unit of the transition.
concerns.quote: A more relevant comparison would be to known energy scales for domain-wall motion, oxygen-vacancy migration, or the latent heat per formula unit

concerns.concern: The 1.7 mA operating point should be marked in Fig. 5b. It may lie below I₁, making it unclear whether a filament forms there, which matters for interpreting Fig. 4.
concerns.quote: It appears to lie near or below I₁, so it is unclear whether a filament forms at 1.7 mA.

concerns.concern: The irradiation geometry is contradictory: central region versus global irradiation. This matters because irradiation-driven filament localization bears on the learned filament path.
concerns.quote: p. 2 says "central 5×5 µm region irradiated," whereas the Methods say "devices were globally irradiated."

concerns.concern: The normalization of ΔG(n,n+1) to [0, 1] is not defined; the raw G values and the procedure should be given.
concerns.quote: the normalization to [0, 1] is not defined. The raw G values and the normalization procedure should be given.

concerns.concern: The cycling protocol is ambiguous. On time, off time and the timing of the 1 s exposure within the on phase should be specified.
concerns.quote: "Turned on and off for 3 s" could mean 3 s on and 3 s off, or a 3 s period.

concerns.concern: The Joule-heating argument should be made quantitative with an estimate of the local temperature rise at each current, allowing direct comparison with the Arrhenius τ(T).
concerns.quote: An estimate of the local temperature rise at 0.26, 1.7 and 4 mA, from a thermal model or a calibration of the Bragg peak shift

concerns.concern: Fig. 3b has only ~300 s of pre-switching data; a longer baseline is needed to support the claim that the initial configuration is immediately erased.
concerns.quote: would be stronger with a longer pre-switching baseline, as in Fig. 3a.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature τ is inconsistent between the text (8000 ± 3000 s, also misnamed 'decay rates') and Fig. 2c (81,000 ± 3000 s).
concerns.quote: the text gives "8000 ± 3000 s" (also misnamed "decay rates"), while Fig. 2c gives τ = 81,000 ± 3000 s.

concerns.concern: The 4 mA τ is inconsistent between the text (150,000 s) and Fig. 3h (160,000 s).
concerns.quote: the text gives 150,000 ± 50,000 s, while Fig. 3h gives 160,000 ± 50,000 s.

concerns.concern: The sub-threshold current is given as 0.26 mA in the figures but 0.27 mA in the text.
concerns.quote: given as 0.26 mA (Fig. 3, Fig. 4 legend) but 0.27 mA in the text on p. 5.

concerns.concern: The definition of the aging-time lines is wrong: they satisfy t₁ + t₂ = 2t_age, not t₁ + t₂ = t_age.
concerns.quote: satisfy t₁ + t₂ = 2t_age, not t₁ + t₂ = t_age

concerns.concern: The text refers to an inset in Fig. 3i that does not exist.
concerns.quote: the text refers to "The inset (orange data)" in Fig. 3i; there is no inset.

concerns.concern: Calling β the 'stretching exponent' when β > 1 is a misnomer; 'compressing' or 'shape' exponent would be more accurate.
concerns.quote: Calling β the "stretching exponent" when β > 1 is a misnomer

concerns.concern: Eq. 2 uses τ as a dummy time variable, which clashes with τ as the relaxation time.
concerns.quote: Eq. 2 uses τ as a dummy time variable, which clashes with τ as the relaxation time.

concerns.concern: Eq. 3 is described as a single exponential, but it is a stretched/compressed exponential.
concerns.quote: Eq. 3 is described as a "single exponential," but it is a stretched/compressed exponential.

concerns.concern: The G(t₁,t₂) maps are called three-dimensional plots but are two-dimensional color plots.
concerns.quote: The G(t₁,t₂) maps are two-dimensional color plots, not "three-dimensional plots."

concerns.concern: The 20 nm domain size should specify direction (in-plane or out-of-plane) and account for finite-thickness and strain broadening of the peak width.
concerns.quote: should specify the direction (in-plane or out-of-plane). The width likely includes finite-thickness (45 nm) and strain broadening.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1e schematic places the stochastic-to-deterministic transition near 100 cycles, inconsistent with the data (onset ~200, saturation ~1000).
concerns.quote: Fig. 1e shows the stochastic-to-deterministic transition centred near 100 cycles, inconsistent with the data

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1 caption describes panels d and e only as 'center' and 'bottom' rather than by panel letter.
concerns.quote: panels d and e are described only as "center" and "bottom" panels; use the panel letters.
